facts.text: PMBOK and PRINCE2 are published bodies of project-management method, while agile is a family of practices that delivers work in short, repeated cycles; all three are general frameworks for running projects.
facts.quote: PMBOK, PRINCE2 and agile are general frameworks for how to run projects: two are published bodies of project-management method, and agile is a family of practices that delivers work in short, repeated cycles.

facts.text: The Project Management Institute (PMI) is a United States professional body.
facts.quote: The Project Management Institute (PMI) is a United States professional body.

facts.text: PMI's Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), seventh edition (2021), collects accepted practice, including rolling-wave planning and risk-register practice.
facts.quote: Its Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide, seventh edition, 2021) collects accepted practice, including rolling-wave planning and risk-register practice.

entities.name: Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge

facts.text: PRINCE2, seventh edition (2023), published by PeopleCert, is a method of United Kingdom government origin built around stages, defined roles and a project initiation document.
facts.quote: PRINCE2 (seventh edition, 2023, published by PeopleCert) is a method of United Kingdom government origin built around stages, defined roles and a project initiation document.

facts.text: Cooper's 2016 Agile-Stage-Gate hybrid brought agile methods into physical product development.
facts.quote: Cooper's 2016 Agile-Stage-Gate hybrid brought them into physical product development

facts.text: The F-35's maker credited integration of an automatic ground-collision avoidance function to agile development and reuse of earlier work.
facts.quote: the F-35 integration of an automatic ground-collision avoidance function was credited by its maker to agile development and reuse of earlier work [Chapters 2, 12].

facts.text: The booklet labels the PMBOK and PRINCE2 sources as expert opinion.
facts.quote: It labels the PMBOK and PRINCE2 sources as expert opinion.

facts.text: Rolling-wave planning is documented practice, but the booklet found no outcome evidence for rolling-wave planning.
facts.quote: Rolling-wave planning is documented practice with no outcome evidence found.

facts.text: No planning method of any kind has consistent outcome evidence for programs like the heavy off-road collision-mitigation virtual-validation program.
facts.quote: No planning method of any kind has consistent outcome evidence for programs like this one.

facts.text: Knowledge before commitment is the best-supported underlying planning principle; United States Government Accountability Office (GAO) audits link the principle correlationally, rather than causally, to better cost and schedule outcomes.
facts.quote: The best-supported underlying principle is knowledge before commitment, which United States Government Accountability Office (GAO) audits link, correlationally, to better cost and schedule outcomes.

facts.text: The booklet recommends layering planning methods rather than choosing one: systems-engineering verification and validation planning as the backbone, evidence-based gates for governance, readiness levels only for novel elements, assumption-based and discovery-driven planning for uncertainty, reference class forecasting and schedule-risk analysis for time, and a roadmap for communication.
facts.quote: systems-engineering verification and validation planning as the backbone, evidence-based gates for governance, readiness levels for novel elements only, assumption-based and discovery-driven planning for uncertainty, reference class forecasting and schedule-risk analysis for time

facts.text: PMBOK and PRINCE2 are useful templates for document structure, and the booklet recommends borrowing from them.
facts.quote: PMBOK and PRINCE2 are useful as templates for document structure, and the booklet lists them among the sources to borrow from

facts.text: Neither PMBOK nor PRINCE2 tells a safety reviewer whether a simulation can be trusted; simulation credibility frameworks, rather than project methods, answer that question.
facts.quote: neither tells a safety reviewer whether a simulation can be trusted; that question is answered by the credibility frameworks, not by project method [Chapter 12].
